title: The Cecil Hotel and nightly jam sessions in New York
summary: Musicians stayed at the hotel, and every night Don Byas, Lester Young, Dizzy, Eddie Davis and others jammed downstairs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: O.K., moving ahead a little bit, just to fill in, when you first came to New York, you staid in the Cecil Hotel. I wonder just what the scene was like, if you could say a little more about that: who else was staying there and what kind of things were going on, especially...
Well anybody would be subject to be staying there, you know. It's whoever was in town. But, you know, you could eat there...you could eat downstairs, they

had restaurants. And the main thing was that every night there was a jam session. And, if you were off, and naturally you staid upstairs, you come downstairs and you might see anybody there. There was Don Byas and Lester and Dizzy and Eddie Lockjaw Davis, Paul Gonzalves. You can name 'em. All the guys were there all the time. So every night was a different night. It was stimulating.
